Some kind of powerful positive Energy you will feel..
results.text:
Approximately 2 km from Tribhuvan International Airport lies Pashupatinath temple, an ancient lord Shiva temple .The location is known as Gaushala. When you enter into the area through the entrance from Gaushala stop you will find local vendors and a Nepal SBI ATM van for the convenience of the visitors from Outside.Moving towards the main temple you will find flower and Prasad sellers you can also buy a Sankh(a sea shell that is blown during Puja in Hindu culture) ,and a Rudraksh garland. Moving past these stalls there are vendors exchanging coins for cash.You can exchange some cash for coins. I will tell you later why people buy some coins here. Moving towards the temple you will find concrete paved stairs leading towards the main temple. On the right is the way towards the Aryaghat (cremation area ) on the banks of Bagmati river.Since Only Hindus are allowed in the main temple non Hindus don't have much to see towards the main temple Yah ofcourse you can take pictures from far. If you are a Hindu you can move towards the temple. There a free counter you can safely keep your shoes and chappals in a bag and you get a token that is to be shown when you return to get your belongings back.Till the gate mobile and cameras are allowed.Even non Hindus can come till this spot. You have submit your camera here.Mobile are allowed to keep in your pocket .But usage is strictly prohibited.
Inside the temple you fill find huge Nandi in the main area. lord Pashupatinath temple is built in the Nepalese pagoda style of architecture.Beautifully carved wooden rafters,Golden Pinnacle and doors covered  with silver sheets. Inside there is a huge black Shiva linga .I was able to get view of it from all four sides. You will experience some very powerful vibration out there. There are other temple to visit around the main temple. From the back area you can see the view of Aryaghat below there are open display of cremation ceremony of the dead on the banks of Bagmati river. From this place you will see a top of a temple on Aryaghat with coins on it. It is believed that if you throw or release a coin from above and if it rests on the pinnacle of the temple below. You will get your wish fulfilled.There are many lengends and beliefs out here .Other temple of basukinath and scluptures of budhanilkantha and Hanuman can be seen here. You will get a good crowd if you visit the temple on Monday .In the month of Shrawan ( end of July to mid of Auga
ust).On the day of Shivaratri about 1 million people visit this place and the numbers are increasing every year.

results.title: Fascinating Hindy spiritual site
results.text: Non Hindus are not allowed in the main temple, but you can still see and photograph a lot of incredible places from the surrounding areas.  Entrance is expensive by Nepalese standards (Rs1000 / $10) but less than you'd pay in many other countries.  Expect a guide to attach himself to you and then ask for a tip at the end.

results.title: Temple
results.text: Sacred sight and temple. Worth a visit, very important place of worship for hindus. Great views from the back side of the temple. It is old and historical sacred place. I recommend it.

results.title: Very moving
results.text: I took my sons here to experience a funeral in another culture. The whole business seemed pretty business like for the first two funerals. Then a family came to bury their mother/husband, and with the sincere grieving, and the care that they took with their departed mother/wife's body, the way they lavished her with the red powder (forgot what it's called), washed her face and lips over and over, and let her feet sit for a good long while in the river, you got the sense of how people here part with their loved ones. It was a good experience for my sons, especially in seeing the difference in the families. People mourn differently, but we felt that the last woman was more deeply loved.

results.title: One of the Jyotirlinga's. Must visit if you get chance
results.text: We were lucky to shift our plans to Kathmandu last moment from Pokhara. If you believe and it's possible then do visit this place for Lord Shiva. We didnt know about temple timings and reached only 2 mins before the closing time in afternoon. Lucky I would say.

results.title: A holy site but not for the faint hearted
results.text:
Second holy site for the Hindus after Varanasi, it is a must visit for prayers but also for cremation of departed ones.
If you feel uncomfortable with witnessing a cremation, please refrain to visit. Otherwise it is very interesting to witness the entire ceremony.
Stroll along the ghat on the opposite side of the cremation pyres.
Beautiful Shiva shrines all aligned to form a kind of tunnel.
The main temple is not accessible to anyone but priests but Hindus can visit the courtyard which has a huge golden bull.

results.title: Holy temple
results.text:
There are lots of monkeys in the temple premises, so be careful with your 'prasad'. There's cremation grounds right behind Pashupatinath, apparently it's a touristy thing for foreigners to do, however I was put off by it.
Temple aarti is something to wait for. I brought my parents for it, and there were quite pleased.

results.title: Entry for Non-Hindus Prohibited
results.text:
To maintain religious purity, non Hindus are forbidden entry into this sacred precinct! At the entrance this breaks down to a Racial Barrier, as Indian Christians can just walk in, because, “they look like Hindus!”
While I respect the concept of purity and sanctity, I know no pure men of any religion, and I know that a civil society can only progress as an inclusive one!
On the other hand religious prejudice is even a right in America!
